text:
alex_h: FYI CI microbench failed on PR #20421 — threshold diff +4.7% on kv-prefetch path. attaching CI snippet

sam: ugh, saw that. microbench that regresses is `kv_warmup_micro` (95th).

mira: can you paste the CI link? did this happen after the kernel-selector change in #20390?

alex_h: https://ci.internal/redwood/20421/units
logs:
```
FAIL: perf_threshold: kv_warmup_micro > baseline (4.7% > 2.0%)
flamegraph: s3://ci-artifacts/20421/kv_warmup_micro/flame.svg
```

sam: flamegraph shows extra time in prefetch worker and kernel autoselect path. looks like extra spin in `kv_prefetch_queue` after commit `e3a7f2c`.

prateek: running bisect between `main~10` and `main`. starting binary search on CI.

ci-bot: bisect job started: https://ci.internal/bisect/7865

prateek: bisect narrowed to commit `b4c9d1f` (PR #20390) — kernel-selector heuristics tweak. perf delta reproduced locally on p3-small.

jen: interesting — that PR adjusted affinity thresholds to prefer small-kernel on seq<=64, but we also changed prefetch wake policy. combined they might trigger hysteresis.

mira: can we try reverting the prefetch wake change only in a branch and run microbench? maybe it's the interaction.

prateek: created branch `prefetch-wake-revert-20421` and kicked off CI.

ci-bot: rebuild passed unit tests, microbench run queued.

alex_h: microbench result: regression gone. threshold within noise (+0.3%). Looks like prefetch-wake change caused the kv cache to miss more often on short sequences.

sam: ok confirm root cause: the prefetch wakerate incremented the batch timer, causing earlier prefetch evictions. that dropped kv_hit from 0.84->0.79.

mira: mitigation: revert prefetch wake change in main, and open follow-up PR to adjust kernel-selector to be robust to prefetch timing.

jen: creating revert PR now. tagging @oncall-runtime for rollout approval.

ci-bot: PR 20430 (revert: prefetch-wake) created, CI started.

prateek: adding perf regression test to prevent this class: test that asserts kv_hit >= 0.82 on synthetic short-seq workload.

alex_h: thanks all. plan: merge revert once green, then iterate on kernel heuristics in a smaller canary.

sam: +1

mira: assigning follow-ups to @prateek and @jen. will post postmortem after rollout.
